Natural_Language: This part addresses broad security requirements that apply to acquisitions of products and services. It outlines policies and procedures for managing information security and supply chain security when acquiring products and services that include, but are not limited to, information and communications technology (ICT).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_000_a_1: This part addresses broad security requirements for acquisitions of products and services; P_40_000_a_2: This part outlines policies and procedures for managing information security when acquiring products and services; P_40_000_a_3: This part outlines policies and procedures for managing supply chain security when acquiring products and services; P_40_000_a_4: Covered products and services include but are not limited to ICT
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Conjunction captures all four elements. Non-exclusive list means ICT is illustrative, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: See parts 24 and 46 for more policies and procedures related to managing information security and supply chain security.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_000_b_1: Part 24 contains additional information/supply chain security policies; P_40_000_b_2: Part 46 contains additional information/supply chain security policies
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference directive. External dependencies on Parts 24 and 46.

Natural_Language: Information and supply chain policies and procedures that are unrelated to security are covered in other parts of the FAR (e.g., part 22 for labor and human trafficking risks).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_000_c: Non-security information and supply chain policies are covered in other FAR parts
Validation_Notes: Scope limitation. Part 22 cited as illustrative. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Scope of part. Part 40 addresses information security and supply chain security for acquisitions, references other parts for additional and non-security coverage.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_000: Scope of Part 40
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for 40.000 scope provisions.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk, as defined in 41 U.S.C. 4713(k), means the risk that any person may sabotage, maliciously introduce unwanted functionality, extract data, or otherwise manipulate the design, integrity, manufacturing, production, distribution, installation, operation, maintenance, disposition, or retirement of covered articles so as to surveil, deny, disrupt, or otherwise manipulate the function, use, or operation of the covered articles or information stored or transmitted on the covered articles.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_001_a: Risk that any person may sabotage, introduce unwanted functionality, extract data, or manipulate covered articles across their lifecycle; P_40_001_b: Purpose is to surveil, deny, disrupt, or manipulate function/use/operation of covered articles or their information
Validation_Notes: Statutory definition from 41 U.S.C. 4713(k). Two conjuncts: risk activity and intent. Both must be present.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk information includes information that describes or identifies: Functionality and features of covered articles, including access to data and information system privileges.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_1: Supply chain risk information includes functionality and features of covered articles, including access to data and information system privileges
Validation_Notes: Category 1 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_2: Supply chain risk information includes the user environment where a covered article is used or installed

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_3: Supply chain risk information includes the ability of a source to produce and deliver covered articles as expected
Validation_Notes: Category 3 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk information includes information that describes or identifies: Foreign control of, or influence over, a source or covered article.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_4: Supply chain risk information includes foreign control of, or influence over, a source or covered article
Validation_Notes: Category 4 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Validation_Notes: Category 6 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_7: Supply chain risk information includes market alternatives to the covered source

Validation_Notes: Category 9 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_10: Supply chain risk information includes security, authenticity, and integrity of covered articles and their supply and compilation chains
Validation_Notes: Category 10 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk information includes information that describes or identifies: Capacity to mitigate risks identified.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_11: Supply chain risk information includes capacity to mitigate risks identified
Validation_Notes: Category 11 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk information includes information that describes or identifies: Factors that may reflect upon the reliability of other supply chain risk information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101_12: Supply chain risk information includes factors that may reflect upon the reliability of other supply chain risk information
Validation_Notes: Category 12 of 13 supply chain risk information types. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Supply chain risk information includes information that describes or identifies: Any other considerations that would factor into analyzing the security, integrity, resilience, quality, trustworthiness, or authenticity of covered articles or sources.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_101: Supply chain risk information definition encompasses 13 enumerated categories
Validation_Notes: Parent. All 13 categories are conjunctive. Non-exhaustive (includes but is not limited to).

Natural_Language: Executive agencies must share relevant supply chain risk information with the Federal Acquisition Security Council if the executive agency determines there is a reasonable basis to conclude a substantial supply chain risk associated with a source or covered article exists (see 41 CFR 201-1.201).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_102_a: Executive agency determines reasonable basis for substantial supply chain risk; P_40_102_b: Agency shares relevant supply chain risk information with FASC
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conditional. "Must" creates binding obligation triggered by reasonable basis determination. References 41 CFR 201-1.201 (external to FAR). HIGH-RISK for implication direction.

Natural_Language: American Security Drone Act-covered foreign entity means an entity included on a list developed and maintained by the Federal Acquisition Security Council (FASC) and published in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov (section 1822 of Pub. L. 118-31, 41 U.S.C. 3901 note prec.).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_ASDA: ASDA-covered foreign entity is an entity on the FASC-maintained list published in SAM
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Entity status determined by inclusion on FASC list in SAM. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Backhaul means intermediate links between the core network, or backbone network, and the small subnetworks at the edge of the network (e.g., connecting cell phones/towers to the core telephone network). Backhaul can be wireless (e.g., microwave) or wired (e.g., fiber optic, coaxial cable, Ethernet).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_backhaul_a: Backhaul is intermediate links between core/backbone network and edge subnetworks; P_40_201_backhaul_b: Backhaul can be wireless or wired
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Two components: functional description and medium types. Examples are illustrative.

Natural_Language: Business operations means engaging in commerce in any form, including by acquiring, developing, maintaining, owning, selling, possessing, leasing, or operating equipment, facilities, personnel, products, services, personal property, real property, or any other apparatus of business or commerce.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_busops: Business operations means engaging in commerce in any form across enumerated activities
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Broad, non-exhaustive ("including") list of commercial activities. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered application means the social networking service TikTok or any successor application or service developed or provided by ByteDance Limited or an entity owned by ByteDance Limited.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covapp_a: Covered application is TikTok; P_40_201_covapp_b: Covered application includes any successor app/service by ByteDance or ByteDance-owned entity
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Disjunction: either TikTok itself OR any ByteDance successor satisfies the definition.

Natural_Language: Covered article, as defined in 41 U.S.C. 4713(k), means information technology (including cloud computing), telecommunications equipment or service, processing of information on Federal or non-Federal systems subject to CUI requirements, or hardware/systems/devices/software/services with embedded or incidental IT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covart: Covered article definition encompasses four categories
Validation_Notes: Parent definition. Disjunctive: any one of four categories qualifies as covered article.

Natural_Language: Covered article includes information technology, as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11101, including cloud computing services of all types.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covart_1: IT as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11101, including all cloud computing
Validation_Notes: First category. References IT definition also in 40.201. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered article includes telecommunications equipment or telecommunications service, as defined in section 3 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 153).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covart_2: Telecom equipment or service per 47 U.S.C. 153
Validation_Notes: Second category. Statutory cross-reference. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered article includes the processing of information on a Federal or non-Federal information system, subject to the requirements of the Controlled Unclassified Information program (see 32 CFR part 2002).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covart_3: Information processing on Federal/non-Federal systems subject to CUI program
Validation_Notes: Third category. CUI program linkage. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered article includes hardware, systems, devices, software, or services that include embedded or incidental information technology.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covart_4: Hardware/systems/devices/software/services with embedded or incidental IT
Validation_Notes: Fourth category. Broadest category capturing incidental IT. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered foreign country means The People's Republic of China.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covfc: Covered foreign country is the People's Republic of China
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Single named country. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered telecommunications equipment or services encompasses four categories of prohibited telecommunications and video surveillance items.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covtel: Covered telecom definition with four disjunctive categories
Validation_Notes: Parent definition. Disjunctive: any one category satisfies the definition.

Natural_Language: Covered telecommunications equipment or services includes telecommunications equipment produced by Huawei Technologies Company or ZTE Corporation (or any subsidiary or affiliate of such entities).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covtel_1: Telecom equipment by Huawei or ZTE (including subsidiaries/affiliates)
Validation_Notes: First category. Named entities: Huawei, ZTE. Extends to subsidiaries and affiliates. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered telecommunications equipment or services includes, for the purpose of public safety, security of Government facilities, physical security surveillance of critical infrastructure, and other national security purposes, video surveillance and telecommunications equipment produced by Hytera Communications Corporation, Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Company, or Dahua Technology Company (or any subsidiary or affiliate of such entities).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covtel_2_a: Purpose is public safety, government facility security, critical infrastructure surveillance, or national security; P_40_201_covtel_2_b: Equipment produced by Hytera, Hikvision, or Dahua (including subsidiaries/affiliates)
Validation_Notes: Second category. Purpose-limited: only applies when used for enumerated security purposes. Named entities: Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua.

Natural_Language: Covered telecommunications equipment or services includes telecommunications or video surveillance services provided by such entities or using such equipment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covtel_3: Services provided by named entities or using their equipment
Validation_Notes: Third category. Extends prohibition from equipment to services by same entities. Depends on categories 1 and 2 for entity identification. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Covered telecommunications equipment or services includes telecommunications or video surveillance equipment or services produced or provided by an entity that the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence or the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, reasonably believes to be an entity owned or controlled by, or otherwise connected to, the government of a covered foreign country.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_covtel_4_a: SecDef (consulting DNI or FBI Director) reasonably believes entity is owned/controlled by or connected to covered foreign country government; P_40_201_covtel_4_b: Entity produces/provides telecom or video surveillance equipment or services
Validation_Notes: Fourth category. Catch-all: requires SecDef determination of foreign government connection. "Reasonably believes" is a lower evidentiary threshold. Depends on covered foreign country definition (PRC).

Natural_Language: FASCSA order means any order issued under FASCSA requiring removing covered articles from executive agency information systems or excluding named sources/articles from procurement actions, as described in 41 CFR 201-1.303(d) and (e).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_FASCSA: FASCSA order definition with three issuing authorities
Validation_Notes: Parent definition. Three types based on issuing authority. Disjunctive.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of Homeland Security may issue FASCSA orders that apply to civilian agencies, to the extent not covered by paragraph (2) or (3). This type may be referred to as a DHS FASCSA order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_FASCSA_1: DHS Secretary issues FASCSA orders for civilian agencies (residual jurisdiction)
Validation_Notes: First FASCSA order type. DHS has residual civilian agency jurisdiction. Atomic.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of Defense may issue FASCSA orders that apply to the Department of Defense (DoD) and national security systems other than sensitive compartmented information systems. This type may be referred to as a DoD FASCSA order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_FASCSA_2: SecDef issues FASCSA orders for DoD and non-SCI national security systems
Validation_Notes: Second type. DoD jurisdiction over DoD and non-SCI NSS. Atomic.

Natural_Language: The Director of National Intelligence (DNI) may issue FASCSA orders that apply to the intelligence community and sensitive compartmented information systems, to the extent not covered by paragraph (2). This type may be referred to as a DNI FASCSA order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_FASCSA_3: DNI issues FASCSA orders for IC and SCI systems (not covered by DoD)
Validation_Notes: Third type. DNI jurisdiction over IC and SCI. Residual to DoD. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Federal Acquisition Security Council (FASC) means the Council established under 41 U.S.C. 1322(a).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_FASC: FASC is the council per 41 U.S.C. 1322(a)
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Statutory cross-reference. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Information technology, as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11101(6), means equipment or interconnected systems used in automatic data/information handling by executive agencies or contractors, includes computers and ancillary equipment, but excludes equipment acquired incidental to Federal contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_IT: IT definition with three components (scope, inclusions, exclusion)
Validation_Notes: Parent definition. Three conjunctive components define the scope.

Natural_Language: Information technology means any equipment or interconnected system or subsystem of equipment, used in the automatic acquisition, storage, analysis, evaluation, manipulation, management, movement, control, display, switching, interchange, transmission, or reception of data or information by the executive agency, if the equipment is used by the executive agency directly or is used by a contractor under a contract that requires its use or requires its use to a significant extent.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_IT_1_a: Equipment used in automatic data/info handling by executive agency; P_40_201_IT_1_b: Equipment used directly by agency or by contractor under contract requiring such use
Validation_Notes: Core IT definition. Equipment must be for data handling AND either direct agency use or contractor use under contract. Two pathways for contractor use: required use OR significant use.

Natural_Language: Information technology includes computers, ancillary equipment (including imaging peripherals, input, output, and storage devices necessary for security and surveillance), peripheral equipment designed to be controlled by the central processing unit of a computer, software, firmware and similar procedures, services (including support services), and related resources.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_IT_2: IT includes computers, ancillary/peripheral equipment, software, firmware, services, and related resources
Validation_Notes: Inclusive list expanding IT scope. Non-exhaustive. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Information technology does not include any equipment acquired by a Federal contractor incidental to a Federal contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_IT_3: IT excludes equipment acquired by contractor incidental to Federal contract
Validation_Notes: Exclusion from IT definition. Negation captures the carve-out. Limits scope to prevent over-inclusion of incidental contractor equipment.

Validation_Notes: IC member 8 of 12. Atomic.

Validation_Notes: IC member 9 of 12. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Kaspersky Lab-covered article means any hardware, software, or service meeting any of three criteria related to Kaspersky Lab-covered entities.

Validation_Notes: Parent. Any one criterion satisfies. Depends on Kaspersky entity definition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLart_1: Developed or provided by Kaspersky Lab-covered entity
Validation_Notes: First criterion. Direct development or provision. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Kaspersky Lab-covered article includes any item that includes hardware, software, or service developed or provided in whole or in part by a Kaspersky Lab-covered entity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLart_2: Includes items developed/provided in whole or part by Kaspersky entity
Validation_Notes: Second criterion. Partial inclusion. Broadens scope beyond direct products. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Kaspersky Lab-covered article includes any item that contains components using hardware or software developed in whole or in part by a Kaspersky Lab-covered entity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLart_3: Contains components with Kaspersky-developed hardware/software

Natural_Language: Kaspersky Lab-covered entity means Kaspersky Lab, any successor, any entity controlling/controlled by/under common control with Kaspersky Lab, or any entity majority-owned by Kaspersky Lab.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLent: Kaspersky entity definition with four disjunctive criteria
Validation_Notes: Parent. Any one criterion satisfies.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLent_1: Kaspersky Lab itself
Validation_Notes: Entity criterion 1 of 4. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLent_2: Any successor entity including name changes (e.g., "Kaspersky")
Validation_Notes: Entity criterion 2 of 4. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Kaspersky Lab-covered entity includes: Any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Kaspersky Lab.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_KLent_3: Any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Kaspersky Lab
Validation_Notes: Entity criterion 3 of 4. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_margSudan: Two categories of marginalized Sudan populations
Validation_Notes: Parent. Conjunctive: both groups included in definition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_margSudan_1: Adversely affected groups in Darfur Act section 8(c) regions
Validation_Notes: First group. Statutory cross-reference. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_margSudan_2: Marginalized areas in Northern Sudan per section 4(9)
Validation_Notes: Second group. Statutory cross-reference. Atomic.

Natural_Language: National security system, as defined in 44 U.S.C. 3552, means any information system used or operated by or on behalf of an agency meeting either of two criteria.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_NSS: National security system definition with two disjunctive criteria
Validation_Notes: Parent. Either criterion qualifies a system as NSS.

Natural_Language: National security system includes systems whose function, operation, or use involves intelligence activities, cryptologic activities related to national security, command and control of military forces, equipment integral to weapons systems, or is critical to direct fulfillment of military or intelligence missions, but excludes routine administrative and business applications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_NSS_1_a: System involves intelligence, crypto, C2, weapons, or critical military/intel missions; P_40_201_NSS_1_b: System is not for routine admin/business applications
Validation_Notes: First criterion. Must meet functional test AND not be excluded by admin/business carve-out.

Natural_Language: National security system includes systems protected at all times by procedures established for information specifically authorized under Executive order or Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_NSS_2: System always protected by classified information procedures per EO or statute
Validation_Notes: Second criterion. Classification-based qualification. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Sensitive compartmented information means classified information concerning or derived from intelligence sources, methods, or analytical processes, which is required to be handled within formal access control systems established by the Director of National Intelligence.

Natural_Language: Sensitive compartmented information system means a national security system authorized to process or store sensitive compartmented information.

Validation_Notes: Definitional. Bright-line 50% ownership test. Includes indirect ownership. Atomic.

Validation_Notes: Definitional. Statutory cross-reference. Key element: no possibility of direct human intervention. Atomic.

Atomic_Propositions: P_40_201_UAS_a: Unmanned aircraft; P_40_201_UAS_b: Associated elements including communication links and control components required for safe/efficient NAS operation
Validation_Notes: Definitional. UAS is broader than UA: includes all associated elements. Depends on UA definition.

Validation_Notes: Prohibition formalized as negation. Scope/exceptions in clause 52.240-91.

Natural_Language: Upon determination of false certification at 52.240-90(f)(1)(ii) or (f)(1)(iii), the agency must take one or more remedies. The contracting officer terminates the contract in accordance with part 49, or for commercial items, part 12.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_204_4_b_1_a: False certification determined; P_40_204_4_b_1_b: CO terminates contract per Part 49 or Part 12
Validation_Notes: Iran remedies use "must take one or more" unlike Sudan "may" -- this is mandatory, not discretionary. At least one remedy required. Termination is one of three options. HIGH-RISK.

Natural_Language: The suspending and debarring official suspends the contractor in accordance with part 9.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_204_4_b_2_a: False certification determined; P_40_204_4_b_2_b: SDO suspends contractor per Part 9
Validation_Notes: Mandatory remedy option. Part of "must take one or more" framework. Suspension per Part 9.

Natural_Language: The suspending and debarring official debars the contractor for a period of at least two years in accordance with part 9.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_204_4_b_3_a: False certification determined; P_40_204_4_b_3_b: SDO debars contractor for minimum 2 years per Part 9
Validation_Notes: Mandatory remedy option. Note: Iran requires MINIMUM 2 years debarment vs. Sudan MAXIMUM 3 years. Significantly harsher enforcement.

Natural_Language: Iran remedies for false certification: agency must take one or more of termination, suspension, or debarment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_204_4_b: Iran false certification mandatory remedies
Validation_Notes: Parent. Disjunction because "one or more" means at least one required. Unlike Sudan (all permissive), Iran remedies are mandatory.

Natural_Language: This subpart provides policies and procedures for safeguarding classified information and Federal contract information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_300_a: Subpart 40.3 covers safeguarding classified information and FCI
Validation_Notes: Scope statement. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Part 27, Patents, Data, and Copyrights, contains policy and procedures for safeguarding classified information in patent applications and patents.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_300_b: Part 27 covers classified info safeguarding in patent context
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference. External dependency on Part 27. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Scope of subpart 40.3: safeguarding classified information and FCI.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_300: Subpart 40.3 scope
Validation_Notes: Parent for subpart scope.

Natural_Language: Covered contractor information system means an information system that is owned or operated by a contractor that processes, stores, or transmits Federal contract information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_301_CCIS_a: Information system owned or operated by contractor; P_40_301_CCIS_b: System processes, stores, or transmits Federal contract information
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Both elements required: contractor ownership/operation AND FCI handling. Depends on FCI definition.

Natural_Language: Federal contract information means information, not intended for public release, that is provided by or generated for the Government under a contract to develop or deliver a product or service to the Government, but not including information provided by the Government to the public (such as that on public Web sites) or simple transactional information, such as that necessary to process payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_301_FCI_a: Information not intended for public release, provided by or generated for Government under contract; P_40_301_FCI_b: Excludes government-to-public information and simple transactional information
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Inclusion criterion AND exclusion carve-out. Negation captures the "not including" exclusions.

Natural_Language: Information means any communication or representation of knowledge such as facts, data, or opinions in any medium or form, including textual, numerical, graphic, cartographic, narrative, or audiovisual (CNSSI 4009).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_301_info: Any communication or representation of knowledge in any medium or form
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Broadest possible scope. CNSSI 4009 source. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Information system means a discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information (44 U.S.C. 3502).
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_301_IS: Discrete set of info resources organized for info handling (per 44 U.S.C. 3502)
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Statutory cross-reference. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Safeguarding means measures or controls that are prescribed to protect information systems.
Atomic_Propositions: P_40_301_safeguarding: Prescribed measures or controls to protect information systems
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Depends on information system definition. Atomic.

Natural_Language: This section applies to all acquisitions, including acquisitions of commercial products or commercial services, other than commercially available off-the-shelf items, when a contractor's information system may contain Federal contract information.
